predecessors.name: Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic
predecessors.text: the Erivan Governorate, where the Armenian National Council 'declared Armenia's independence' on 28 May 1918 after the Transcaucasian federation fell

successors.name: Armenian Soviet Socialist Republic
successors.text: the republic 'Sovietised' on 2 December 1920; 'most of Zangezur gained by Soviet Armenia' (war page)

successors.name: Republic of Mountainous Armenia
successors.text: Zangezur, listed in the infobox as a successor 'Republic of Mountainous Armenia'

successors.name: Republic of Turkey
successors.text: the Kars region: the city occupied on 30 October 1920, ceded by the Treaty of Alexandropol of 3 December 1920

ledger.x: 28 May 1918: the Armenian National Council declares Armenia's independence.
21 May 1918: the Ottoman offensive in Armenia; at Abaran, Karakilisa and Sardarabad 'local Armenian forces emerged victorious'.
4 June 1918: the Treaty of Batum ends the fighting and leaves Armenia 11,396 km2.
November 1918: after the Armistice of Mudros (30 October) the Ottoman army leaves the Erivan Governorate and Armenia grows by about 16,000 km2.
Late November 1918: Andranik's offensive into Karabakh.
7 December 1918: Armenian-Georgian skirmishes begin ('Skirmishes began on 7 December').
31 December 1918: the ceasefire takes effect 'at midnight on 31 December'.
June 1919: Drastamat Kanayan's Armenian troops take Nakhichevan city and destroy the Republic of Aras; Azerbaijani and Ottoman troops retook it in July.
10 August 1919: ceasefire over Nakhichevan ('On 10 August 1919, a ceasefire was signed'); the dispute itself went on to 1920, so this ends only the 1919 fighting.
28 April 1920: the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic ceases to exist when the Soviet 11th Army occupies it; the Armenian claim passes to Soviet Azerbaijan.
April-May 1920: the Soviet 11th Army 'conquered Karabakh in May 1920'; Nakhichevan 'was Sovietized later in 1920'.
28 September 1920: the Turkish army under Karabekir invades Armenia.
30 October 1920: in the invasion begun on 28 September the Turkish army under Karabekir occupies the city of Kars, 'supposed to be impregnable', leaving its 25,000 defenders disorganised.
November 1920: Zangezur 'ceded by Azerbaijan to Armenia' as a 'symbol of friendship'; the war ends.
3 December 1920: Karabekir 'imposed on Armenia the Treaty of Alexandropol'; Armenia 'was confined to the province of Yerevan, thereby ceding Kars, Nakhchivan, and Surmalu'.
2 December 1920: 'due to the threat of a Soviet ultimatum' the government hands power to the Soviets; the Revkom had proclaimed Soviet rule on 29 November.

wars.name: Battle of Sardarabad and the Ottoman offensive of May 1918
wars.outcome: Armenian forces won at Abaran, Karakilisa and Sardarabad; the Treaty of Batum of 4 June 1918 left Armenia 11,396 km2.

wars.name: Armeno-Georgian War
wars.outcome: Skirmishes from 7 December 1918 and a ceasefire from midnight on 31 December; the page opened gives no change of frontier.

wars.name: Armenian-Azerbaijani war (1918-1920)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive (infobox, 30 March 1918 - 28 November 1920): 'Most of Zangezur gained by Soviet Armenia'; the Karabakh and Nakhichevan disputes settled for Soviet Azerbaijan.

wars.name: Turkish-Armenian War
wars.outcome: Turkey invaded on 28 September 1920, occupied the city of Kars on 30 October and imposed the Treaty of Alexandropol on 3 December 1920, ceding 'Kars, Nakhchivan, and Surmalu' and leaving Armenia 27,000-30,044 km2.

certainty.note: Most frontiers were contested or occupied (Karabakh, Zangezur, Nakhichevan, Kars, the Georgian border); only the Batum line of 4 June 1918 and the Alexandropol line of 3 December 1920 were treaty lines, and the page does not describe them.
